issues.legal_issue: A prior decision is not per incuriam merely because a later court considers that it failed to address an aspect of the matter.
material_facts: An earlier Full Bench had decided the validity and effect of the relevant consolidation provisions.
A later Full Bench treated the earlier decision as per incuriam because it had not considered whether the consolidation authorities were courts of limited jurisdiction.
The later Full Bench did not base that finding on the earlier court having overlooked a binding authority or a statutory provision.
The earlier and later Full Bench decisions reached conflicting conclusions on the issues before them.
issues.conclusion: The later Full Bench misapplied the doctrine of per incuriam; the earlier decision could not be disregarded on the ground that it had not considered a possible aspect of the matter.
issues.legal_principle: Under the doctrine of per incuriam, a decision may be treated as such where the court decided in ignorance of a binding precedent or a statutory provision. A mere failure to consider an argument or possible aspect is insufficient. The Court relied on Halsbury's Laws of England; Govt. of Andhra Pradesh v. B. Satyanarayana Rao, which explains that the doctrine applies where a binding precedent or statute was omitted; State of U.P. v. Synthetics and Chemicals Ltd., on decisions rendered in ignorance of binding authority; and Fuerst Day Lawson Ltd. v. Shivaraj V. Patil, which requires an obvious and material oversight of statutory or obligatory authority.

rule.if: later_coordinate_bench and earlier_binding_decision and later_bench_identified_only_an_unconsidered_aspect and not binding_authority_overlooked

predicates.later_coordinate_bench: A later bench of coordinate jurisdiction considered an issue previously decided by another bench of coordinate jurisdiction.
predicates.earlier_binding_decision: An earlier decision of coordinate jurisdiction addressed the same issue and was binding on the later bench.
predicates.later_bench_identified_only_an_unconside: The later bench relied only on the earlier court's failure to consider a possible aspect or argument.
predicates.binding_authority_overlooked: The earlier court decided the issue in ignorance of a binding precedent or a statutory provision.

issues.definition: When a later coordinate bench confronts a binding earlier decision and identifies only an unconsidered aspect, without an overlooked binding authority, the earlier decision remains binding.

issues.legal_issue: A coordinate bench that disagrees with a binding decision of another coordinate bench must follow it or refer the issue to a larger bench rather than decide the issue inconsistently.
material_facts: An earlier Full Bench had decided the same or similar legal issues as the later Full Bench.
The later Full Bench disagreed with the earlier decision and treated it as non-binding without establishing a valid basis for applying the doctrine of per incuriam.
The later Full Bench issued conclusions conflicting with the earlier Full Bench's conclusions.
issues.conclusion: The later Full Bench was not entitled to disregard the earlier decision; it had to follow that decision or seek resolution by a larger bench. The impugned judgment was set aside and the matter remanded for reconsideration in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Judicial discipline and certainty require a bench of coordinate jurisdiction that disagrees with an earlier decision to follow it or refer the matter to a larger bench, rather than leave conflicting decisions in force. A prior decision ceases to state correct law where a subsequent change in law is shown. The Court relied on Dr. Vijay Laxmi Sadho v. Jagdish and Pradip Chandra Parija v. Pramod Chandra Patnaik, which set out the proper course when benches disagree, and Govt. of Andhra Pradesh v. B. Satyanarayana Rao, concerning the effect of a subsequent change in law.

rule.if: later_coordinate_bench and earlier_binding_decision and later_bench_disagrees and not subsequent_change_in_law

predicates.later_coordinate_bench: A later bench of coordinate jurisdiction considers an issue decided by an earlier bench of coordinate jurisdiction.
predicates.earlier_binding_decision: An earlier decision of coordinate jurisdiction addressed the same issue and was binding on the later bench.
predicates.later_bench_disagrees: The later bench considers the earlier decision incorrect on the issue.
predicates.subsequent_change_in_law: A change in law after the earlier decision has displaced its rule.

issues.definition: When a later coordinate bench disagrees with a binding earlier decision and no subsequent change in law has displaced it, the later bench must follow the earlier decision or refer the issue for resolution by a larger bench.
